source_arguments.name: RHTower.BeurlingRegularIntegers.integral_cexp_mul_regularDensity
source_arguments.statement:
theorem integral_cexp_mul_regularDensity {β γ δ : ℝ} (A : ℕ)
    (hδ1 : δ < 1) (hβ1 : β < 1) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < s.re) :
    (∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), Complex.exp (-(s * t)) * (regularDensity β γ δ A t : ℂ)) =
      (Complex.log (s - (β : ℂ) - (γ : ℂ) * I) - Complex.log (s - 1)) +
        ((Complex.log (s - (β : ℂ) + (γ : ℂ) * I) - Complex.log (s - (δ : ℂ))) +
          ((A : ℂ) - 1) * (Complex.log s - Complex.log (s - (δ : ℂ))))
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem integral_cexp_mul_regularDensity {β γ δ : ℝ} (A : ℕ)
    (hδ1 : δ < 1) (hβ1 : β < 1) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < s.re) :
    (∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), Complex.exp (-(s * t)) * (regularDensity β γ δ A t : ℂ)) =
      (Complex.log (s - (β : ℂ) - (γ : ℂ) * I) - Complex.log (s - 1)) +
        ((Complex.log (s - (β : ℂ) + (γ : ℂ) * I) - Complex.log (s - (δ : ℂ))) +
          ((A : ℂ) - 1) * (Complex.log s - Complex.log (s - (δ : ℂ))))
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  have h1 : 0 < (s - (1 : ℂ)).re := by
    simpa using re_pos_of_one_lt (a := 1) le_rfl hs
  have hδ : 0 < (s - (δ : ℂ)).re := re_pos_of_one_lt hδ1.le hs
  have h0 : 0 < s.re := lt_trans one_pos hs
  obtain ⟨hm, hp⟩ := re_pos_sub_conj (β := β) (γ := γ) hβ1 hs
  have hsplit :
      (∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), Complex.exp (-(s * t)) * (regularDensity β γ δ A t : ℂ)) =
        ∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ),
          ((Complex.exp (-((s - 1) * t)) - Complex.exp (-((s - β - γ * I) * t))) / t +
          ((Complex.exp (-((s - δ) * t)) - Complex.exp (-((s - β + γ * I) * t))) / t +
            ((A : ℂ) - 1) *
              ((Complex.exp (-((s - δ) * t)) - Complex.exp (-(s * t))) / t))) := by
    refine setIntegral_congr_fun measurableSet_Ioi ?_
    intro t ht
    exact cexp_mul_regularDensity β γ δ A s ht
  have hint3 : IntegrableOn
      (fun t : ℝ => ((A : ℂ) - 1) *
        ((Complex.exp (-((s - (δ : ℂ)) * t)) - Complex.exp (-(s * t))) / t)) (Ioi (0 : ℝ)) := by
    have := integrableOn_frullani hδ h0
    exact this.const_mul _
  have hint2 : IntegrableOn
      (fun t : ℝ => (Complex.exp (-((s - (δ : ℂ)) * t)) -
          Complex.exp (-((s - (β : ℂ) + (γ : ℂ) * I) * t))) / t +
        ((A : ℂ) - 1) *
          ((Complex.exp (-((s - (δ : ℂ)) * t)) - Complex.exp (-(s * t))) / t))
      (Ioi (0 : ℝ)) := (integrableOn_frullani hδ hp).add hint3
  rw [hsplit, integral_add (integrableOn_frullani h1 hm) hint2,
    integral_add (integrableOn_frullani hδ hp) hint3,
    integral_const_mul, integral_frullani h1 hm, integral_frullani hδ hp,
    integral_frullani hδ h0]

source_arguments.statement:
theorem integral_cexp_mul_adjoinedDensity (β γ : ℝ) {s : ℂ} (hs : β < s.re) :
    (∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), Complex.exp (-(s * t)) * (adjoinedDensity β γ t : ℂ)) =
      Complex.log (s - (β : ℂ) - (γ : ℂ) * I) + Complex.log (s - (β : ℂ) + (γ : ℂ) * I) -
        2 * Complex.log (s - (β : ℂ))
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem integral_cexp_mul_adjoinedDensity (β γ : ℝ) {s : ℂ} (hs : β < s.re) :
    (∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), Complex.exp (-(s * t)) * (adjoinedDensity β γ t : ℂ)) =
      Complex.log (s - (β : ℂ) - (γ : ℂ) * I) + Complex.log (s - (β : ℂ) + (γ : ℂ) * I) -
        2 * Complex.log (s - (β : ℂ))
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  have h0 := re_sub_pos (β := β) hs
  have h1 := re_sub_sub_pos (β := β) (γ := γ) hs
  have h2 := re_sub_add_pos (β := β) (γ := γ) hs
  have hsplit :
      (∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), Complex.exp (-(s * t)) * (adjoinedDensity β γ t : ℂ)) =
        ∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ),
          ((Complex.exp (-((s - (β : ℂ)) * t)) -
            Complex.exp (-((s - (β : ℂ) - (γ : ℂ) * I) * t))) / t +
          (Complex.exp (-((s - (β : ℂ)) * t)) -
            Complex.exp (-((s - (β : ℂ) + (γ : ℂ) * I) * t))) / t) := by
    refine setIntegral_congr_fun measurableSet_Ioi ?_
    intro t ht
    exact cexp_mul_adjoinedDensity β γ s ht
  rw [hsplit, integral_add (integrableOn_frullani h0 h1) (integrableOn_frullani h0 h2),
    integral_frullani h0 h1, integral_frullani h0 h2]
  ring

source_arguments.name: RHTower.BeurlingLogarithmicCounting.integral_weighted_primeDensity
source_arguments.statement:
theorem integral_weighted_primeDensity (g : ℝ) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < s.re) :
    (∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), Complex.exp (-(s * t)) * (primeDensity g t : ℂ)) =
      (Complex.log (s - 2 / 3 - (g : ℂ) * Complex.I) - Complex.log (s - 1)) +
      (Complex.log (s - 2 / 3 + (g : ℂ) * Complex.I) - Complex.log s) +
      (Complex.log (s + 1 / 3) - Complex.log s)
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem integral_weighted_primeDensity (g : ℝ) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < s.re) :
    (∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), Complex.exp (-(s * t)) * (primeDensity g t : ℂ)) =
      (Complex.log (s - 2 / 3 - (g : ℂ) * Complex.I) - Complex.log (s - 1)) +
      (Complex.log (s - 2 / 3 + (g : ℂ) * Complex.I) - Complex.log s) +
      (Complex.log (s + 1 / 3) - Complex.log s)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  obtain ⟨h1, h0, hm, hp, ha⟩ := positive_rates g hs
  rw [setIntegral_congr_fun measurableSet_Ioi (fun t ht => weighted_primeDensity_split g s ht)]
  unfold frullaniKernel
  have h12 : IntegrableOn (fun t : ℝ =>
      (Complex.exp (-((s - 1) * t)) - Complex.exp (-((s - 2 / 3 - (g : ℂ) * Complex.I) * t))) / t +
      (Complex.exp (-(s * t)) - Complex.exp (-((s - 2 / 3 + (g : ℂ) * Complex.I) * t))) / t)
      (Ioi 0) := (integrableOn_frullani h1 hm).add (integrableOn_frullani h0 hp)
  rw [integral_add h12 (integrableOn_frullani h0 ha), integral_add (integrableOn_frullani h1 hm)
    (integrableOn_frullani h0 hp), integral_frullani h1 hm, integral_frullani h0 hp,
    integral_frullani h0 ha]

theorem integral_dampedFrullani {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :

      = Real.log (Real.sqrt (ε ^ 2 + 1))
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  have hare : (0 : ℝ) < (1 : ℂ).re := by simp
  have hbre : (0 : ℝ) < ((ε : ℂ) - Complex.I).re := by
    simp only [Complex.sub_re, Complex.ofReal_re, Complex.I_re, sub_zero]
    exact hε
  have hfr := integral_frullani hare hbre
  have hint := integrableOn_frullani hare hbre
  have hcomm := Complex.reCLM.integral_comp_comm hint
  simp only [Complex.reCLM_apply] at hcomm
  have hre : ∀ t ∈ Ioi (0 : ℝ),
      ((Complex.exp (-((1 : ℂ) * (t : ℂ))) - Complex.exp (-(((ε : ℂ) - Complex.I) * (t : ℂ))))
        / (t : ℂ)).re
        = (Real.exp (-t) - Real.exp (-(ε * t)) * Real.cos t) / t := by
    intro t ht
    have hr : (-(((ε : ℂ) - Complex.I) * (t : ℂ))).re = -(ε * t) := by
      simp only [Complex.neg_re, Complex.mul_re, Complex.sub_re, Complex.sub_im,
        Complex.ofReal_re, Complex.ofReal_im, Complex.I_re, Complex.I_im]
      ring
    have him : (-(((ε : ℂ) - Complex.I) * (t : ℂ))).im = t := by
      simp only [Complex.neg_im, Complex.mul_im, Complex.sub_re, Complex.sub_im,
        Complex.ofReal_re, Complex.ofReal_im, Complex.I_re, Complex.I_im]
      ring
    have h1 : (Complex.exp (-((1 : ℂ) * (t : ℂ)))).re = Real.exp (-t) := by
      rw [show (-((1 : ℂ) * (t : ℂ))) = ((-t : ℝ) : ℂ) from by push_cast; ring,
        ← Complex.ofReal_exp, Complex.ofReal_re]
    have h2 : (Complex.exp (-(((ε : ℂ) - Complex.I) * (t : ℂ)))).re
        = Real.exp (-(ε * t)) * Real.cos t := by
      rw [Complex.exp_re, hr, him]
    rw [div_ofReal_re, Complex.sub_re, h1, h2]
  have hleft : (∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ),
      (Real.exp (-t) - Real.exp (-(ε * t)) * Real.cos t) / t)
      = (∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ),
          (Complex.exp (-((1 : ℂ) * (t : ℂ)))
            - Complex.exp (-(((ε : ℂ) - Complex.I) * (t : ℂ)))) / (t : ℂ)).re := by
    rw [← hcomm]
    exact (MeasureTheory.setIntegral_congr_fun measurableSet_Ioi hre).symm
  rw [hleft, hfr, Complex.log_one, sub_zero, Complex.log_re]
  congr 1
  rw [Complex.norm_eq_sqrt_sq_add_sq]
  simp

theorem tendsto_intervalIntegral_real_frullani
    {A B : ℝ} (hA : 0 < A) (hB : 0 < B) :
    Tendsto
      (fun p : ℝ × ℝ ↦ ∫ t in p.1..p.2,
        t⁻¹ * (Real.exp (-(A * t)) - Real.exp (-(B * t))))
      ((nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0)) ×ˢ atTop)
      (nhds (Real.log (B / A)))
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem tendsto_intervalIntegral_real_frullani
    {A B : ℝ} (hA : 0 < A) (hB : 0 < B) :
    Tendsto
      (fun p : ℝ × ℝ ↦ ∫ t in p.1..p.2,
        t⁻¹ * (Real.exp (-(A * t)) - Real.exp (-(B * t))))
      ((nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0)) ×ˢ atTop)
      (nhds (Real.log (B / A)))
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  let g : ℝ → ℝ := fun t ↦
    t⁻¹ * (Real.exp (-(A * t)) - Real.exp (-(B * t)))
  have hpoint (t : ℝ) : g t =
      ((Complex.exp (-((A : ℂ) * t)) -
        Complex.exp (-((B : ℂ) * t))) / (t : ℂ)).re := by
    have hexpA : (Complex.exp (-((A : ℂ) * t))).re =
        Real.exp (-(A * t)) := by
      rw [show -((A : ℂ) * t) = ((-(A * t) : ℝ) : ℂ) by
        push_cast
        rfl]
      exact Complex.exp_ofReal_re _
    have hexpB : (Complex.exp (-((B : ℂ) * t))).re =
        Real.exp (-(B * t)) := by
      rw [show -((B : ℂ) * t) = ((-(B * t) : ℝ) : ℂ) by
        push_cast
        rfl]
      exact Complex.exp_ofReal_re _
    by_cases ht : t = 0
    · simp [g, ht]
    · simp [g, hexpA, hexpB, div_eq_mul_inv, mul_comm]
      rw [← mul_assoc, mul_inv_cancel₀ ht, one_mul]
      exact Or.inl rfl
  have hcomplex := integrableOn_frullani
    (a := (A : ℂ)) (b := (B : ℂ)) (by simpa using hA) (by simpa using hB)
  have hreal : IntegrableOn g (Ioi (0 : ℝ)) := by
    have hre := hcomplex.re
    change Integrable g (volume.restrict (Ioi (0 : ℝ)))
    convert hre using 1
    funext t
    exact hpoint t
  have hlim := tendsto_intervalIntegral_Ioi_two_sided hreal
  have hfr := integral_frullani
    (a := (A : ℂ)) (b := (B : ℂ)) (by simpa using hA) (by simpa using hB)
  have hvalue : (∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), g t) = Real.log (B / A) := by
    calc
      (∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), g t) =
          ∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ),
            ((Complex.exp (-((A : ℂ) * t)) -
              Complex.exp (-((B : ℂ) * t))) / (t : ℂ)).re := by
            congr 1
            funext t
            exact hpoint t
      _ = ((∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ),
            (Complex.exp (-((A : ℂ) * t)) -
              Complex.exp (-((B : ℂ) * t))) / (t : ℂ)) : ℂ).re :=
        integral_re hcomplex
      _ = (Complex.log (B : ℂ) - Complex.log (A : ℂ)).re :=
        congrArg Complex.re hfr
      _ = Real.log (B / A) := by
        rw [Complex.sub_re, Complex.log_re, Complex.log_re,
          Real.log_div hB.ne' hA.ne']
        simp [abs_of_pos hA, abs_of_pos hB]
  rw [hvalue] at hlim
  simpa only [g] using hlim

by
  set G : ℝ → ℝ := fun t => -(Real.exp (-t) * Real.log t) with hGdef
  set G' : ℝ → ℝ := fun t => Real.log t * Real.exp (-t) - Real.exp (-t) / t with hG'def
  have hcont : ContinuousWithinAt G (Set.Ici 1) 1 := by
    refine ContinuousWithinAt.neg ?_
    exact ((Real.continuous_exp.comp continuous_neg).continuousWithinAt).mul
      (Real.continuousAt_log (by norm_num)).continuousWithinAt
  have hderiv : ∀ x ∈ Set.Ioi (1 : ℝ), HasDerivAt G (G' x) x := by
    intro x hx
    have hx0 : x ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt (lt_trans zero_lt_one hx)
    have h1 : HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => Real.exp (-t)) (-Real.exp (-x)) x := by
      have := (Real.hasDerivAt_exp (-x)).comp x (hasDerivAt_neg x)
      simpa [Function.comp_def] using this
    have h2 : HasDerivAt Real.log x⁻¹ x := Real.hasDerivAt_log hx0
    have h3 := (h1.mul h2).neg
    refine h3.congr_deriv ?_
    rw [hG'def]
    field_simp
    ring
  have hint : IntegrableOn G' (Set.Ioi (1 : ℝ)) volume := by
    rw [hG'def]
    exact integrableOn_log_mul_exp_Ioi_one.sub integrableOn_exp_neg_div_Ioi_one
  have hlim : Tendsto G atTop (nhds 0) := by
    refine squeeze_zero_norm' (a := fun t : ℝ => t * Real.exp (-t)) ?_ ?_
    · filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop (1 : ℝ)] with t ht
      have ht0 : (0 : ℝ) < t := lt_of_lt_of_le zero_lt_one ht
      have hlog : 0 ≤ Real.log t := Real.log_nonneg ht
      have hlt : Real.log t ≤ t := le_trans (Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos ht0) (by linarith)
      rw [hGdef]
      simp only [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_neg, abs_mul,
        abs_of_nonneg (Real.exp_nonneg (-t)), abs_of_nonneg hlog]
      nlinarith [Real.exp_nonneg (-t)]
    · have := Real.tendsto_pow_mul_exp_neg_atTop_nhds_zero 1
      simpa using this
  have hftc := MeasureTheory.integral_Ioi_of_hasDerivAt_of_tendsto hcont hderiv hint hlim
  have hG1 : G 1 = 0 := by rw [hGdef]; simp
  rw [hG1, sub_zero] at hftc
  rw [hG'def] at hftc
  rw [MeasureTheory.integral_sub integrableOn_log_mul_exp_Ioi_one
    integrableOn_exp_neg_div_Ioi_one] at hftc
  rw [frullaniTail]
  linarith

by

    Filter.eventually_of_mem
      (mem_nhdsWithin_of_mem_nhds (Iic_mem_nhds (by norm_num))) (fun x hx => hx)
  have hheadmeas : ∀ ε : ℝ, AEStronglyMeasurable
      (fun t : ℝ => (Real.exp (-t) - Real.exp (-(ε * t)) * Real.cos t) / t)
      (volume.restrict (Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1)) := by
    intro ε
    refine ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable ?_ measurableSet_Ioc
    intro t ht
    have ht0 : 0 < t := ht.1
    exact ContinuousAt.continuousWithinAt
      (ContinuousAt.div (by fun_prop) continuousAt_id (ne_of_gt ht0))
  have hheadDCT : Tendsto
      (fun ε : ℝ => ∫ t in Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1,
        (Real.exp (-t) - Real.exp (-(ε * t)) * Real.cos t) / t)
      (nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0)) (nhds gaussCosineHead) := by
    have hconst : Integrable (fun _ : ℝ => (3 : ℝ)) (volume.restrict (Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1)) :=
      continuous_const.integrableOn_Ioc
    refine MeasureTheory.tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence
      (fun _ : ℝ => (3 : ℝ)) ?_ ?_ hconst ?_
    · filter_upwards [self_mem_nhdsWithin] with ε _
      exact hheadmeas ε
    · filter_upwards [self_mem_nhdsWithin, hsmall] with ε hε hε1
      have hεpos : (0 : ℝ) < ε := hε
      filter_upwards [ae_restrict_mem measurableSet_Ioc] with t ht
      have ht0 : (0 : ℝ) < t := ht.1
      rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_div, abs_of_pos ht0, div_le_iff₀ ht0]
      have := abs_exp_sub_cos_le (le_of_lt ht0) ht.2 hεpos hε1
      nlinarith
    · filter_upwards [ae_restrict_mem measurableSet_Ioc] with t ht
      have ht0 : (0 : ℝ) < t := ht.1
      have hexp : Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => Real.exp (-(ε * t))) (nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0)) (nhds 1) := by
        have hcont : ContinuousAt (fun ε : ℝ => Real.exp (-(ε * t))) 0 := by fun_prop
        have h1 : Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => Real.exp (-(ε * t)))
            (nhdsWithin (0 : ℝ) (Ioi 0)) (nhds (Real.exp (-(0 * t)))) :=
          hcont.tendsto.mono_left nhdsWithin_le_nhds
        simpa using h1
      have hnum : Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => Real.exp (-t) - Real.exp (-(ε * t)) * Real.cos t)
          (nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0)) (nhds (Real.exp (-t) - Real.cos t)) := by
        have := (tendsto_const_nhds (x := Real.exp (-t))
          (f := nhdsWithin (0 : ℝ) (Ioi 0))).sub (hexp.mul_const (Real.cos t))

      (fun ε : ℝ => (∫ t in Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1,
          (Real.exp (-t) - Real.exp (-(ε * t)) * Real.cos t) / t)
        + frullaniTail - dampedCosTail ε)
      (nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0)) (nhds (gaussCosineHead + frullaniTail - cosTailValue)) :=
    (hheadDCT.add tendsto_const_nhds).sub tendsto_dampedCosTail
  have hLHS : Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => Real.log (Real.sqrt (ε ^ 2 + 1)))
      (nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0)) (nhds 0) := by
    have hcont : ContinuousAt (fun ε : ℝ => Real.log (Real.sqrt (ε ^ 2 + 1))) 0 := by

      · fun_prop
      · simp
    have h1 : Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => Real.log (Real.sqrt (ε ^ 2 + 1)))

  have hEq : Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => Real.log (Real.sqrt (ε ^ 2 + 1)))

    refine hRHS.congr' ?_

    have hεpos : (0 : ℝ) < ε := hε
    have hsplit : Set.Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1 ∪ Set.Ioi (1 : ℝ) = Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ) :=
      Set.Ioc_union_Ioi_eq_Ioi zero_le_one
    have hdisj : Disjoint (Set.Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1) (Set.Ioi (1 : ℝ)) := by
      rw [Set.disjoint_left]
      intro x hx hx'
      exact absurd hx' (not_lt.mpr hx.2)

# Continuous countermodel with an exact logarithmic counting remainder

- **ID:** CONTINUOUS-BEURLING-LOG-ERROR-AUDIT
- **Stage:** 3-formalized / not_new_scientific_knowledge
- **Type:** source-class audit and explicit auxiliary construction; not an RH architecture
- **Source:** `BeurlingRationalRealizability`, `BeurlingRegularIntegersOffLineZeros`,
  `FrullaniIntegral`, `MonomialLaplaceComplex`; current statements inspected.
- **Novelty:** not established; treat as an application of classical continuous Beurling constructions.

## Why this is needed

`regular_integers_do_not_constrain_zeros` chooses its model after the error exponent. Its Lean
statement proves positivity of a continuous logarithmic density and a rational transform identity,
not a counting asymptotic. Several descriptions reverse that quantifier order and infer universal
requirements on RH proof methods. Correct those descriptions independently of whether this repair
works. Continuous countermodels cannot eliminate a method whose additional discrete hypotheses
they do not satisfy.

## Concrete repair and paper proof

For real `g`, define

```
c = 4/27 + g^2/3,       r = 4/27 + 4g^2/3,
w_g(t) = (exp(t)+2-2 exp(2t/3) cos(g t)-exp(-t/3))/t,       t>0,
Z_g(s) = ((s-2/3)^2+g^2)(s+1/3)/((s-1)s^2),
J_g(t) = r exp(t) + (1-r) - r t - c t^2/2,                 t>=0,
j_g(t) = r(exp(t)-1)-c t.
```

The existing exponential factorization at `t/3` gives
`exp(t)+2-2 exp(2t/3)-exp(-t/3)>=0`. Adding
`2 exp(2t/3)(1-cos(g t))` proves `w_g>=0`. Its numerator vanishes at zero and is differentiable,
so the density is locally integrable at zero. Three Frullani terms, with pole parameters `1,0,0`
and zero parameters `2/3+i g,2/3-i g,-1/3`, give

```
exp(integral_(t>0) exp(-s t) w_g(t) dt) = Z_g(s),           Re(s)>1.
```

`J_g(0)=1`, `J_g'=j_g`, and `j_g(t)>=0` on `t>=0`: use `exp(t)-1>=t` and `r-c=g^2`.
Thus `J_g` counts a positive continuous measure with a unit atom at zero in logarithmic
coordinates. The elementary transforms of `1,t,exp(t)` yield

```
1 + integral_(t>0) exp(-s t) j_g(t) dt
  = 1 + r/(s-1) - r/s - c/s^2 = Z_g(s),                   Re(s)>1.
```

These identities explicitly pair the positive counting density with the positive logarithmic-prime
density at the level of their transforms. Lean proves the two integrability statements and transform
identities; it does not invoke a formal measure-uniqueness or convolution-exponential theorem. The exact counting formula is `N_g(x)=J_g(log x)` for `x>=1`, hence
`N_g(x)-r x = 1-r-r log x-c(log x)^2/2`. It has `O((log x)^2)` remainder and therefore, for this
**one fixed model**, `O(x^e)` for every `e>0`. When `g!=0`, `2/3+i g` is a genuine nonreal zero:
the denominator is nonzero there. The family is continuous; it is not a sequence of primes or of
unit-weight integers, and no functional equation is claimed.

## Exact formal result

`formal/GaloisForLFunctions/RHTower/BeurlingLogarithmicCounting.lean` contains 19 public theorems.
The premise-free `explicit_continuous_countermodel` instantiates `g=1` and packages:

- nonnegativity of both densities on their stated domains;
- the counting primitive as `1 + integral_0^t j(u) du`;
- integrability and both transform identities for every `Re(s)>1`;
- the exact remainder `-13/27-(40/27)log x-(13/54)(log x)^2` for `x>=1`;
- `o(x^e)` remainder for every `e>0`, with the same counting function;
- the zero at `2/3+i`, its nonzero denominator, and its real and imaginary parts.

Domain quantifiers are part of the closed statement. There is no RH premise, added axiom, numerical
certificate, discrete realization, or claimed functional equation. Local finiteness and the
interpretation through a convolution exponential are paper consequences; the formal interface is
specified by the integral identities above.

## Verification

- Scratch and production `lake env lean` checks passed.
- The comment-corrected older module also passed its direct check.
- `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=1 lake build --old GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.BeurlingLogarithmicCounting`
  passed, rebuilding only the changed older dependency and the new leaf; other dependency jobs
  were cached. No full or umbrella build ran.
- All 19 public theorems passed an imported scratch axiom audit: only `propext`, `Classical.choice`,
  and `Quot.sound`. The private helpers are included transitively in these dependency audits.
- `RHTower.lean` imports the leaf; generated indexes refreshed; repository formal lint passed with
  existing large-file warnings. No mathematical computation was used and no Runpod job was started.

## Consequence for further research

The original arbitrary-zero theorem retains `for every exponent, there exists a model`; this new
fixed-model theorem proves a stronger error statement for zeros at the specified horizontal position
`2/3`. It does not prove arbitrary horizontal placement in a single subpower-error family.

OT YET A ROUTE]

Lean constructs a source-only strict-right height-window Ward bound after functional-
equation absorption. The scale-invariant Hellinger--Cauchy separator has positive mixed entries and
constant self-charge but a divergent balanced Euler diagonal. Cubic log-moment weighting repairs
that exact defect: the zero-side self-charge is `115/(864a^3)`, uniformly positive for every
strict-right displacement, while the literal balanced prime-depth diagonal
`115/(864(e+1)^3p^(e+1)(log p)^2)` is summable. Exact Bohr dephasing deletes distinct-ordinate
cross terms and a budget `N/4` would yield a three-quarters critical-line receiver.

This is a credible new architecture opening, not a route. Lean proves genuine holomorphic height
translation cannot be scalar-normalized into the unitary phases used by the Bohr mean at depths
one and two. Missing are a coefficient-faithful pre-divisor comparison from the cubic Euler source
to the cubic zero energy and a mechanism upgrading the three-quarters endpoint to RH. Frullani/
Laplace Gram kernels, Bohr means, and classical zero-density language provide ancestry; no reviewed
source supplies either missing theorem. No external formalization is selected before a concrete
source-to-zero identity is proposed.

### Cross-route receivers — Deninger divisor-defect traces [NOT A NEW ROUTE]

The corpus constructs an absolutely convergent cubic resolvent defect trace weighted by
`mu-conj(mu)` and proves its identical vanishing equivalent to RH. A three-point version has a
simple-pole detector; on the Euler half-plane its companion mixed twisted trace is exactly an
honest pole--Gamma--von-Mangoldt source combination minus the defect. Vanishing for every triple is
again equivalent to RH. Classical resolvent partial fractions and explicit-formula calculus are
parent methods. Local content is the coefficient-exact Deninger/Ward twist, absolute summability,
and pole extraction. Because both defects are formed from the divisor, no reviewed external
theorem turns them into an unconditional pre-zero annihilator. They strengthen L/R diagnostics but
do not create a producer or a literature-to-Lean action.

**Sonin/Route-E seam, not a route.** Lean-proved
`SoninCofinalReporterClockCommutatorSeam.lean` puts the two constructions on one `ell2` source,
proves strong convergence of positive Sonin pullbacks, decomposes the transported Fisher score
into reporter plus a fixed-source-vanishing clock commutator, and constructs a diagonal landing on
Route E's literal prime-labelled one-corner codiagonal. Both converge to `2u/(1+u)^2` and are
eventually positive for `u>0`. No external collision was located for this source-specific
identification. Its consequence is negative for merger design: after scalar landing it cannot
annihilate off-neutral orientation. Lean-proved
`SoninCofinalComplexPhaseOddFisherSplice.lean` now retains that upstream coordinate. One common
cofinal finite schedule transports both `+it` and `-it` phases; their difference tends to
`4it(1-t^2)/(1+t^2)^2`, nonzero for `0<|t|<1`. No completed-Xi physical-metric identification or
global annihilation theorem is proved, so this remains cross-route infrastructure rather than a
new route.

### Cross-route infrastructure — XiC order-one and explicit-formula organ [NOT A NEW ROUTE]

**Local contribution.** Corpus-first audit closes the previously stated growth frontier.
`CompletedZetaGrowth.lean` proves the unconditional global order-one bound;
`XiHadamardGrowth.lean` proves quotient constancy and
`XiC=XiC(0)*xiCanonicalProduct`; `XiZerosInfinite.lean` proves infinite divisor support; and the
heat-shell/canonical-product modules give local shell finiteness and inverse-square summability.
No Cartan detour or separate nontrivial-zero existence proof is missing.

Prime-side glue is also formal. `XiWardInteriorTraceSplit.lean` opens `logDeriv xi` on `Re s>1`
into pole, Gamma, and von Mangoldt L-series terms; `XiGuinandWeilSymmetricContour.lean` identifies
the centered bottom edge with the exact prime--archimedean source, and the finite-contour modules
supply zero-residue receivers. `XiRelativeResolventTrace.lean` already gives the absolutely
convergent centered zero-side partial fraction in resolvent form. Lean-proved
`XiExplicitFormulaLogDeriv.lean` transports it to classical coordinates and glues it to the
arithmetic side, proving a direct multiplicity-exact zero-sum = pole--Gamma--von-Mangoldt identity
on `Re s>1`.

**Literature boundary and action.** Hadamard factorization, Jensen theory, theta Mellin estimates,
canonical-product logarithmic differentiation, and Guinand--Weil contour calculus are classical
parents. Local contribution is their exact certified assembly for the corpus `xi`/`XiC` and route
sockets. Direct classical-coordinate explicit formula is now certified; it is not a missing
mathematical organ. A new route still requires an independent
source-side positivity, coercivity, or cancellation producer.

# EDQ reflected current as positive prefix energy

Stage: 3-formalized; dependency-closed paper proof and Lean verified.
Full chain: Euler deletion → exact complex zero balance → signed arithmetic separation → exclusion of off-line zeros → RH.
RH status: the real current has the exact orientation below. Its annihilation at every zero is not established.

Write r(s)=1-conjugate(s), alpha=2*Re(s)-1, and w_n=(n+1)^alpha. For the literal
modulus-p+1 jumps u_n at s, the reflected jumps are exactly v_n=w_n*u_n. Let
X_N=sum_(n<N)u_n and Y_N=sum_(n<N)v_n. For arbitrary real weights and complex jumps,
put Z_N=w_N*X_N-Y_N. Then

`Z_(n+1)-Z_n=(w_(n+1)-w_n)*X_(n+1)`.

Finite summation by parts, without any zero premise, therefore gives the full complex identity

`C(u,v,N)-C(v,u,N)=w_N*norm(X_N)^2-Y_N*conjugate(X_N)`
`                         -sum_(n<N)(w_(n+1)-w_n)*norm(X_(n+1))^2`.

No imaginary part or diagonal term has been dropped. At an actual nontrivial zero s,
the corpus bounds norm(X_N) by A_p(s)*(N+1)^(-Re(s)); hence the first terminal norm is at
most A_p(s)^2/(N+1). Both ordinary endpoints tend to zero. The previous variation-current
identity then identifies the full reflected arithmetic current with the real prefix-energy limit.

For alpha>0 the weights strictly increase, for alpha<0 they strictly decrease, and for
alpha=0 they are constant. Each squared prefix norm is nonnegative. For every actual
nontrivial modulus (p>0), X_1=1. Therefore the first energy term is exactly 2^alpha-1,
strictly positive or negative with alpha. All further terms have the same weak sign.
The terms have one sign, so convergence of their partial sums proves genuine summability.
The full complex current is exactly the real sum of these terms. Consequently it is real at zeros,
has the sign of Re(s)-1/2, and vanishes exactly on
the critical line. Its positive survivor is the literal source energy, not an assumed Hilbert model.

This does not establish that the full current vanishes at every zero. The imaginary endpoint
equation already proved only gives its imaginary part. An additional source identity or
comparison forcing the real energy to vanish is still necessary for RH. Functional-equation
covariance exchanges partners and reverses the current; it does not identify the two values.

The quantitative right-half floor is `2^(2*Re(s)-1)-1 <= Re(J_p(s))`; on the left half

# T2 natural Abel-wall square-energy no-go

- **ID:** T2-NAT-ABEL-L2-WALL
- **Stage:** 1-in-progress
- **Type:** CONJECTURE
- **Source:** `rh-current-frontier-map.md`, Route T2 literal natural Wold square-energy producer
- **Statement:** For every `t > 1/2`, the literal natural Wold square energy `WoldNatResidualSquareEnergy t` is false.

## Goal
Kill Route T2's entire cofinal square-energy producer.  Its RH gate asks for energy at every
`1/4 < t < 3/4`; nonexistence at any (indeed every) `t > 1/2` makes that premise inconsistent.
The intended proof uses an unconditional Hardy critical-line zeta zero, not RH or any zero-location
hypothesis.

## Gates
- [x] 0 → 1  in-progress: source-pure statement, exact proof chain, corpus/literature audit
- [ ] 1 → 2  fully-proven: complete natural-Abel continuation identity and pole contradiction
- [ ] 2 → 3  formalized: closed Lean theorem, targeted build, axioms and lint audits
- [ ] 3 → 4  publication-ready: standalone theorem, proof, novelty comparison, Lean certificate

## Corpus-derived proof chain
1. Put `R_N = xiHeatCassiniWoldNatResidualLogDiscrepancy N` and
   `F(s) = sum_{N>=1} R_N N^{-s}`.  The energy is exactly weighted `ell^2` membership of `R_N`.
2. If `E(t) < infinity`, `t > 1/2`, Cauchy--Schwarz gives absolute convergence and holomorphy of
   `F` on `Re(s) > 1-t`; in particular at every critical-line point `rho`.
3. Equivalently, the natural Abel current
   `A(s) = sum_{N>=1} R_N (N^{-s}-(N+1)^{-s})` is holomorphic on `Re(s) > -t` and is continuous at
   every translated critical point `s0 = rho-1`.  The sharp majorant on `Re(s)>=-1/2` is
   `C |R_N| N^{-1/2}`; Cauchy--Schwarz reduces it to `E(t)` and `sum N^{-2t}`.
4. Finite Abel summation on the natural cutoff gives, first for `Re(s)>0`,
   `A(s) = WoldCurrent(s) - IntegerLogMesh(s) + boundary`, because
   `R_N-R_{N-1} = WoldNatWeight(N) - (log N-log(N-1))`.
5. Continue the integer logarithmic mesh by subtracting its `1/N` principal term:
   `log(N/(N-1))-1/N = O(N^{-2})`.  Its remainder is holomorphic on `Re(s)>-1`, while the
   principal term is `zeta(s+1)` and is regular at every nonreal `s0=rho-1`.
6. The corpus theorem
   `xiHeatCassiniWoldCriticalLaplaceContinuation_zero_residue` gives residue `-m != 0` for the
   Wold current at every critical-line zero.  Analytic continuation of step 4 therefore forces the
   natural Abel current to have the same nonzero pole at `s0`.
7. Hardy's unconditional critical-zero theorem supplies such a nonreal `rho`.  Steps 3 and 6
   contradict.  Hence `not_woldNatResidualSquareEnergy_of_half_lt` and, immediately, failure of
   the complete cofinal T2 producer.

## Conjecturing loop
- **C1 (failed):** energy directly implies absolute critical prime-edge variation.  Cauchy duality
  exposes a weighted square prime-gap moment, so this reintroduces Route T's open mesh producer.
- **C2 (active):** use every natural cutoff and the natural Abel current.  Its dual is the ordinary
  convergent p-series `sum N^{-2t}`; no prime-gap estimate remains.
- **Positive survivor if endpoint fails:** the same argument is sharp for every `t>1/2`; it does
  not claim the endpoint `t=1/2`, where the dual series becomes harmonic.

## Novelty audit (through 2026-08-30)
- Corpus has the natural square-energy RH gate, the adaptive cubic obstruction only for `t>3/4`,
  the critical Wold pole carrier, and generic square-summable Dirichlet-series holomorphy.  It has
  no natural-cutoff Abel current, no weighted-energy-to-critical-wall theorem, and no `t>1/2`
  no-go.
- Zhao (2025) treats signed first means of the three classical Mertens errors; Bhattacharya,
  Martin, and Simpson (2025) treat correlations and sign distributions of weighted prime-counting
  errors; Brent, Platt, and Trudgian (2021) treat mean square of `psi(x)-x`.  None states the
  discrete Wold residual energy threshold or the natural-Abel pole mechanism above.

## Lean infrastructure required by the proof

import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Basic

/-!
# Finite weighted-barycentric readers

An exact weighted-barycentric packet reader is the projectivization of an additive marked
current.  Multiplication by the total mass recovers that current, so a positive barycentric
normalization preserves scalar zero loci and signs.  This is the reusable algebraic classification
needed by the edge-marked Gamma--Jacobi reader.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

/-- Total mass of a finite marked packet. -/
def finiteBarycentricTotalMass
    {E : Type*} (edges : Finset E) (mass : E → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ e ∈ edges, mass e

/-- Additive mass-weighted current carried by a finite marked packet. -/
def finiteBarycentricCurrent
    {E V : Type*} [AddCommMonoid V] [Module ℝ V]
    (edges : Finset E) (mass : E → ℝ) (value : E → V) : V :=
  ∑ e ∈ edges, mass e • value e

/-- Normalized weighted-barycentric reader of a finite marked packet. -/
def finiteBarycentricReader
    {E V : Type*} [AddCommMonoid V] [Module ℝ V]
    (edges : Finset E) (mass : E → ℝ) (value : E → V) : V :=
  (finiteBarycentricTotalMass edges mass)⁻¹ •
    finiteBarycentricCurrent edges mass value

/-- **Dehomogenization law.**  Multiplication by nonzero total mass recovers the additive marked
current exactly. -/
theorem finiteBarycentricTotalMass_smul_reader
    {E V : Type*} [AddCommMonoid V] [Module ℝ V]
    (edges : Finset E) (mass : E → ℝ) (value : E → V)
    (htotal : finiteBarycentricTotalMass edges mass ≠ 0) :
    finiteBarycentricTotalMass edges mass •
        finiteBarycentricReader edges mass value =
      finiteBarycentricCurrent edges mass value := by
  rw [finiteBarycentricReader, smul_smul,
    mul_inv_cancel₀ htotal, one_smul]

/-- Exact converse classification: a proposed packet value is the barycentric reader exactly
when its mass-weighted lift is the additive marked current. -/
theorem finiteBarycentricReader_eq_iff_totalMass_smul_eq_current
    {E V : Type*} [AddCommMonoid V] [Module ℝ V]
    (edges : Finset E) (mass : E → ℝ) (value : E → V) (v : V)
    (htotal : finiteBarycentricTotalMass edges mass ≠ 0) :
    finiteBarycentricReader edges mass value = v ↔
      finiteBarycentricTotalMass edges mass • v =
        finiteBarycentricCurrent edges mass value := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    rw [← h]
    exact finiteBarycentricTotalMass_smul_reader edges mass value htotal
  · intro h
    rw [finiteBarycentricReader, ← h, smul_smul,
      inv_mul_cancel₀ htotal, one_smul]

/-- A nonzero normalization cannot create or remove a zero of the additive current. -/
theorem finiteBarycentricReader_eq_zero_iff_current_eq_zero
    {E V : Type*} [AddCommMonoid V] [Module ℝ V]
    (edges : Finset E) (mass : E → ℝ) (value : E → V)
    (htotal : finiteBarycentricTotalMass edges mass ≠ 0) :
    finiteBarycentricReader edges mass value = 0 ↔
      finiteBarycentricCurrent edges mass value = 0 := by
  rw [finiteBarycentricReader]
  exact smul_eq_zero.trans (or_iff_right (inv_ne_zero htotal))

/-- Linear observation commutes with finite barycentric normalization. -/
theorem LinearMap.map_finiteBarycentricReader
    {E V W : Type*} [AddCommMonoid V] [Module ℝ V]
    [AddCommMonoid W] [Module ℝ W]
    (L : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) (edges : Finset E) (mass : E → ℝ) (value : E → V) :
    L (finiteBarycentricReader edges mass value) =
      finiteBarycentricReader edges mass (fun e => L (value e)) := by
  simp only [finiteBarycentricReader, finiteBarycentricCurrent,
    map_smul, map_sum]

/-- Negating every marked value negates the packet reader. -/
theorem finiteBarycentricReader_neg
    {E V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V]
    (edges : Finset E) (mass : E → ℝ) (value : E → V) :
    finiteBarycentricReader edges mass (fun e => -value e) =
      -finiteBarycentricReader edges mass value := by
  simp [finiteBarycentricReader, finiteBarycentricCurrent,
    smul_neg, Finset.sum_neg_distrib]

/-- Positive normalization preserves strict positivity of a real additive current. -/
theorem finiteBarycentricReader_pos_iff_current_pos
    {E : Type*} (edges : Finset E) (mass value : E → ℝ)
    (htotal : 0 < finiteBarycentricTotalMass edges mass) :
    0 < finiteBarycentricReader edges mass value ↔
      0 < finiteBarycentricCurrent edges mass value := by
  rw [finiteBarycentricReader]
  exact smul_pos_iff_of_pos_left (inv_pos.mpr htotal)

/-- Positive normalization preserves strict negativity of a real additive current. -/
theorem finiteBarycentricReader_neg_iff_current_neg
    {E : Type*} (edges : Finset E) (mass value : E → ℝ)
    (htotal : 0 < finiteBarycentricTotalMass edges mass) :
    finiteBarycentricReader edges mass value < 0 ↔
      finiteBarycentricCurrent edges mass value < 0 := by
  rw [finiteBarycentricReader]
  exact smul_neg_iff_of_pos_left (inv_pos.mpr htotal)

end

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-- The coefficient-weighted raw prefixes at the phase-adapted depths `N+j`. -/

/-- The coefficient-weighted dyadic top rows.  The coefficient is exactly
`c_j = P_j q^j`; no extra factor `2`, `1/2`, or `1/4` is absorbed here. -/

    (P : ℝ[X]) (q : ℝ) (N d : ℕ) (z : ℂ) : ℝ :=

/-- The existing complex top-row pairing is the real weighted current above, embedded in `ℂ`. -/

/-- The assembled residue current: the all-prime, label-faithful section of channel residues. -/
def gaussChannelResidueCurrent (m : ℕ) : Nat.Primes → ℝ :=
  fun p => gaussChannelResidue m p

/-- The current is strictly positive at every label. -/
theorem gaussChannelResidueCurrent_pos {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (p : Nat.Primes) :
    0 < gaussChannelResidueCurrent m p :=
  gaussChannelResidue_pos hm p

/-- **Weil normalization.**  The `log p`-normalized current is the rational local factor
`(2/m²)·((p-1)/p)^{2m}·(p^m-1)²`. -/
theorem gaussChannelResidueCurrent_mul_log {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (p : Nat.Primes) :
    gaussChannelResidueCurrent m p * Real.log (p : ℝ)
      = 2 / (m : ℝ) ^ 2 * gaussLocalFactorWeight m p * ((p : ℝ) ^ m - 1) ^ 2 := by
  have hp : (1 : ℝ) < (p : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast p.property.one_lt
  have hp0 : (0 : ℝ) < (p : ℝ) := by linarith
  have hlog : Real.log (p : ℝ) ≠ 0 := (Real.log_pos hp).ne'
  have hm0 : ((m : ℝ)) ≠ 0 := by
    have : (0 : ℝ) < (m : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast (show 0 < m by omega)
    exact this.ne'
  rw [gaussChannelResidueCurrent, gaussChannelResidue, gaussLocalFactorWeight, div_pow]
  field_simp

/-- The current reads the left-half carrier orientation positively at every label. -/
theorem gaussChannelResidueCurrent_mul_carrier_pos_of_leftHalf {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m)
    (q : XiZeroCopy) (hhalf : (q.1 : ℂ).re < 1 / 2) (p : Nat.Primes) :
    0 < gaussChannelResidueCurrent m p * sourceZeroHorizontalPrimeCarrier q p :=
  mul_pos (gaussChannelResidueCurrent_pos hm p)
    (sourceZeroHorizontalPrimeCarrier_pos_of_leftHalf q hhalf p)

/-- The current reads the right-half carrier orientation negatively at every label. -/
theorem gaussChannelResidueCurrent_mul_carrier_neg_of_rightHalf {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m)
    (q : XiZeroCopy) (hhalf : 1 / 2 < (q.1 : ℂ).re) (p : Nat.Primes) :
    gaussChannelResidueCurrent m p * sourceZeroHorizontalPrimeCarrier q p < 0 :=
  mul_neg_of_pos_of_neg (gaussChannelResidueCurrent_pos hm p)
    (sourceZeroHorizontalPrimeCarrier_neg_of_rightHalf q hhalf p)

/-- **Radical preservation.**  Weighting the horizontal prime carrier by the assembled residue
current changes no zero set: the weighted carrier vanishes at a label exactly on the critical
line. -/
theorem gaussChannelResidueCurrent_mul_carrier_eq_zero_iff {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m)
    (q : XiZeroCopy) (p : Nat.Primes) :
    gaussChannelResidueCurrent m p * sourceZeroHorizontalPrimeCarrier q p = 0 ↔
      (q.1 : ℂ).re = 1 / 2 := by
  rw [mul_eq_zero]
  constructor
  · intro h
    rcases h with h | h
    · exact absurd h (gaussChannelResidueCurrent_pos hm p).ne'
    · exact (sourceZeroHorizontalPrimeCarrier_eq_zero_iff q p).1 h
  · intro h
    exact Or.inr ((sourceZeroHorizontalPrimeCarrier_eq_zero_iff q p).2 h)

/-- **Reflection through the weighted carrier.**  The current is fixed by the line-conjugate
reflection while the carrier reverses, so the weighted carrier reverses: both orientations stay
alive after weighting by the assembly. -/
theorem gaussChannelResidueCurrent_mul_carrier_reflection {m : ℕ}
    (q : XiZeroCopy) (p : Nat.Primes) :
    gaussChannelResidueCurrent m p *
        sourceZeroHorizontalPrimeCarrier (xiZeroCopyLineConjEquiv q) p
      = -(gaussChannelResidueCurrent m p * sourceZeroHorizontalPrimeCarrier q p) := by
  rw [sourceZeroHorizontalPrimeCarrier_reflection]
  ring

end

/-!
# Terminal composition for the finite theta-tail core current

This module isolates the exact logical composition still needed after the phase-adapted arithmetic
Haar construction.  It deliberately separates two inputs:

* an exact identity writing the raw core current as one normalized reflected-prefix contribution
  plus one normalized weighted top-row contribution;
* a joint selector controlling those two contributions at the same arithmetic cutoff and Haar
  depth.

The first estimate is one-sided and the second is absolute.  If `J = A + R`, then

`J <= A + |R| < epsilon B / 2 + epsilon B / 2 = epsilon B`.

Thus no sign of the top row and no estimate of the completed pieces separately is required.  The
interfaces below are strictly source-facing: they do not assume the raw core-current bound.
-/

open Complex Real MeasureTheory Set Filter Topology Polynomial

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- The minimal integer strictly above the source-parameter degree of the two finite phase
channels attached to the depth-`d` theta-tail core.  The core translation law uses phase depth
`d + 1`, hence degree `2 * (d + 1)`. -/
def xiCTaylorThetaTailCoreProuhetOrder (d : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  2 * (d + 1) + 1

theorem two_mul_succ_lt_xiCTaylorThetaTailCoreProuhetOrder (d : ℕ) :
    2 * (d + 1) < xiCTaylorThetaTailCoreProuhetOrder d := by
  unfold xiCTaylorThetaTailCoreProuhetOrder
  omega

/-- Exact two-term interface expected from the raw-to-reflected current bridge.  The two real
functions are already-normalized contributions: every factor and sign in the raw Haar identity
must be included in them before this interface can be instantiated. -/
def XiCTaylorThetaTailCoreCurrentTwoTermBridge
    (prefixScale topRowScale : ℝ)
    (m : ℕ → ℕ)
    (prefixContribution topRowContribution : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → ℂ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ d N M : ℕ, ∀ z : ℂ,
    0 < z.im → z.im < 1 / 2 → 2 * (d + 1) < m d →
      orientedPolynomialCurrent (xiCTaylorThetaTailCorePolynomial d) z =
        prefixScale * prefixContribution d N M z +
          topRowScale * topRowContribution d N M z

/-- Joint selection interface at one common arithmetic cutoff and Haar depth.  The prefix is
controlled one-sided, while the top row is controlled in absolute value. -/
def XiCTaylorThetaTailCoreCurrentJointSublinearUpper
    (prefixScale topRowScale : ℝ)
    (D : ℕ → ℕ)
    (prefixContribution topRowContribution : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → ℂ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ sigma : ℂ, 0 < sigma.re → sigma.re < 1 / 2 →
    ∀ epsilon : ℝ, 0 < epsilon →
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ N M : ℕ,
        prefixScale *
            prefixContribution
              (D (xiCTaylorAnisotropicScheduleStage sigma n)) N M
              (xiCTaylorAnisotropicCenteredPoint sigma n) <
          ((epsilon / 2) * ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)) *
            Complex.normSq
              ((xiCTaylorPolynomial
                (xiCTaylorOddDegreeSchedule D
                  (xiCTaylorAnisotropicScheduleStage sigma n))).eval
                    (xiCTaylorAnisotropicCenteredPoint sigma n)) ∧
        |topRowScale *
            topRowContribution
              (D (xiCTaylorAnisotropicScheduleStage sigma n)) N M
              (xiCTaylorAnisotropicCenteredPoint sigma n)| <
          ((epsilon / 2) * ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)) *
            Complex.normSq
              ((xiCTaylorPolynomial
                (xiCTaylorOddDegreeSchedule D
                  (xiCTaylorAnisotropicScheduleStage sigma n))).eval
                    (xiCTaylorAnisotropicCenteredPoint sigma n))

/-! ## Concrete finite-arithmetic data

The corrected raw-current audit has three displayed contributions.  The reflected-prefix integral
is `1 / 2` of the returned finite-arithmetic current and the raw correlation has outer factor
`1 / 4`, giving coefficient `1 / 8`.  Both the weighted top row and the surviving finite-translation
current retain coefficient `1 / 4`.  We keep the latter two together as one remainder: estimating
them separately is neither required nor mathematically safe.
-/

/-- Returned reflected-prefix current at the minimal Prouhet order for the local core depth. -/
def canonicalThetaTailCoreFiniteArithmeticPrefixCurrent
    (d N M : ℕ) (z : ℂ) : ℝ :=
  canonicalThetaTailFiniteArithmeticUntruncatedCurrent
    (xiCTaylorThetaTailCoreProuhetOrder d) N M z

/-- Complete coefficient-weighted top row at the same endpoint, depth, and local core degree. -/
def canonicalThetaTailCoreFiniteArithmeticTopRowCurrent
    (d N M : ℕ) (z : ℂ) : ℝ :=
  (canonicalThetaTailFiniteArithmeticWeightedTopRowCurrent
    d (xiCTaylorThetaTailCoreProuhetOrder d) N M z).re

/-- The exact finite-translation current left by reflection transport and replacement of the
finite core kernel by the untruncated phase kernel. -/

critical first-moment summability of the literal selected leading-current kernel integrals. -/
theorem riemannHypothesis_iff_all_topPrefixFiniteEnergyLeadingKernelIntegral_firstMoment_summable :
    RiemannHypothesis ↔ AllPairedEtaTopPrefixFiniteEnergyLeadingKernelIntegralFirstMomentSummable := by
  rw [riemannHypothesis_iff_all_topPrefixFiniteEnergyLeadingFlux_firstMoment_summable]

theorem modularStrip_halfRow_norm_integrals_summable (F : UpperHalfPlane → ℂ)

    (hi : IntegrableOn F modularStrip volume) :
    Summable (fun v : gammaSetHalf => ∫ z : UpperHalfPlane in fd, ‖F (gammaSetMatrix v.1 • z)‖) := by

    funext v
    rw [fdUnfoldTerm]
    exact integral_ofReal

  exact (Complex.summable_ofReal.mp hn).subtype (fun v => v ∈ gammaSetHalf)

/-- The complete admitted half-row sum unfolds with multiplicity one in the original measure. -/
theorem modularStrip_integral_halfRow_sum (F : UpperHalfPlane → ℂ)
    (hper : ∀ (n : ℤ) (z : UpperHalfPlane), F (T^n • z) = F z)
    (hi : IntegrableOn F modularStrip volume) :

/-
Summation of per-mode van der Corput bounds.

The reflected Dirichlet block, after the Euler–Maclaurin sawtooth is Fourier-expanded, becomes a sum
over frequencies `m` of oscillatory integrals `T m`, each bounded by the (weighted) van der Corput
estimate as `‖T m‖ ≤ K/(m+1)²`.  This module supplies the final summation step: such a family is
absolutely summable and `‖∑' m, T m‖ ≤ K·∑' 1/(m+1)²` — a finite constant (`= K·π²/6`).  The
`Σ 1/m²` convergence is what makes the mode sum finite; the `1/m²` per-mode rate comes from the
frequency `2πm` in the phase derivative.
-/
import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators
open MeasureTheory

noncomputable section

namespace RHTower

/-- **Interval-integral interchange of sum and integral** (absolute convergence).  When the family
`f n` is a.e.-strongly measurable and the integrals of the norms are summable
(`∑' n, ∫⁻ ‖f n‖ ≠ ⊤`), the interval integral commutes with the tsum:
`∫_a^b (∑' n, f n x) dx = ∑' n, ∫_a^b f n x dx`.  This is the interval-integral form of
`MeasureTheory.integral_tsum` (absent from mathlib), the tool that carries the Fourier expansion of
the Euler–Maclaurin sawtooth (via the absolutely summable coefficients of the continuous `B₂`) inside
the integral. -/
theorem intervalIntegral_tsum {a b : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b) {f : ℤ → ℝ → ℂ}
    (hmeas : ∀ n, AEStronglyMeasurable (f n) (volume.restrict (Set.Ioc a b)))
    (hsum : ∑' n : ℤ, ∫⁻ x in Set.Ioc a b, ‖f n x‖ₑ ≠ ⊤) :
    ∫ x in a..b, ∑' n : ℤ, f n x = ∑' n : ℤ, ∫ x in a..b, f n x := by
  rw [intervalIntegral.integral_of_le hab, MeasureTheory.integral_tsum hmeas hsum]
  exact tsum_congr (fun n => (intervalIntegral.integral_of_le hab).symm)

theorem summable_and_norm_tsum_le_of_mode_bound {T : ℕ → ℂ} {b : ℕ → ℝ}
    (hb : Summable b) (hbound : ∀ m, ‖T m‖ ≤ b m) :
    Summable T ∧ ‖∑' m, T m‖ ≤ ∑' m, b m := by
  have hsummT : Summable (fun m => ‖T m‖) :=
    hb.of_nonneg_of_le (fun m => norm_nonneg _) hbound
  refine ⟨hsummT.of_norm, ?_⟩
  calc ‖∑' m, T m‖ ≤ ∑' m, ‖T m‖ := norm_tsum_le_tsum_norm hsummT
    _ ≤ ∑' m, b m := Summable.tsum_mono hsummT hb hbound

-- specialized to the 1/m^2 per-mode bound from weighted van der Corput
theorem summable_and_norm_tsum_le_of_inv_sq_bound {T : ℕ → ℂ} {K : ℝ}
    (hbound : ∀ m, ‖T m‖ ≤ K / ((m : ℝ) + 1) ^ 2) :
    Summable T ∧ ‖∑' m, T m‖ ≤ K * ∑' m : ℕ, (1 : ℝ) / ((m : ℝ) + 1) ^ 2 := by
  have hbsum : Summable (fun m : ℕ => (1 : ℝ) / ((m : ℝ) + 1) ^ 2) := by
    have h := (Real.summable_one_div_nat_pow (p := 2)).mpr (by norm_num)
    exact ((summable_nat_add_iff 1).mpr h).congr (fun m => by push_cast; ring)
  have hKbsum : Summable (fun m : ℕ => K / ((m : ℝ) + 1) ^ 2) :=
    (hbsum.mul_left K).congr (fun m => mul_one_div K _)
  obtain ⟨hsummT, hle⟩ := summable_and_norm_tsum_le_of_mode_bound hKbsum hbound
  refine ⟨hsummT, ?_⟩
  calc ‖∑' m, T m‖ ≤ ∑' m : ℕ, K / ((m : ℝ) + 1) ^ 2 := hle
    _ = K * ∑' m : ℕ, (1 : ℝ) / ((m : ℝ) + 1) ^ 2 := by
        rw [show (∑' m : ℕ, K / ((m : ℝ) + 1) ^ 2)
            = ∑' m : ℕ, K * (1 / ((m : ℝ) + 1) ^ 2) from
              tsum_congr (fun m => (mul_one_div K _).symm)]
        exact tsum_mul_left

end RHTower

theorem tendsto_expSubLinear_cardLength_div_rpow {a₀ b₂ D e s : ℝ} (ha₀0 : 0 < a₀)
    (_ha₀1 : a₀ < 1) (_hb₂0 : 0 < b₂) (hb₂1 : b₂ < 1) (hD : 0 ≤ D) (hs : 0 < s) :
    Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => (Real.log x) ^ e
        * Real.exp (D * (Real.log x) ^ (1 - a₀) * Real.log (Real.log x))
        * cardLength b₂ x / x ^ s) atTop (𝓝 0)
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem tendsto_expSubLinear_cardLength_div_rpow {a₀ b₂ D e s : ℝ} (ha₀0 : 0 < a₀)
    (_ha₀1 : a₀ < 1) (_hb₂0 : 0 < b₂) (hb₂1 : b₂ < 1) (hD : 0 ≤ D) (hs : 0 < s) :
    Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => (Real.log x) ^ e
        * Real.exp (D * (Real.log x) ^ (1 - a₀) * Real.log (Real.log x))
        * cardLength b₂ x / x ^ s) atTop (𝓝 0)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  have hmaj := tendsto_logRpow_mul_expSaving (d := (1 : ℝ)) (s := s / 2) (by norm_num)
    (by linarith) e
  have hsmall := tendsto_logMonomial (e := -a₀) (by linarith) 1
  have hbs : Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => (Real.log x) ^ (b₂ - 1)) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
    tendsto_rpow_log_of_neg (by linarith)
  refine squeeze_zero' ?_ ?_ hmaj
  · filter_upwards [Filter.eventually_gt_atTop (1 : ℝ)] with x hx1
    have hlogx : (0 : ℝ) < Real.log x := Real.log_pos hx1
    have h1 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (Real.log x) ^ e := Real.rpow_nonneg hlogx.le e
    have h2 : (0 : ℝ) < x ^ s := Real.rpow_pos_of_pos (by linarith) s
    have h3 : (0 : ℝ) < cardLength b₂ x := cardLength_pos b₂ x
    positivity
  · filter_upwards [Filter.eventually_gt_atTop (1 : ℝ),
      Real.tendsto_log_atTop.eventually_ge_atTop (1 : ℝ),
      Tendsto.eventually_le_const (show (0 : ℝ) < s / (4 * (D + 1)) by positivity) hsmall,
      Tendsto.eventually_le_const (show (0 : ℝ) < s / 4 by positivity) hbs] with x hx1 hlog1 hsm hbm
    have hx0 : (0 : ℝ) < x := by linarith
    have hlogx : (0 : ℝ) < Real.log x := Real.log_pos hx1
    have hnn : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (Real.log x) ^ e := Real.rpow_nonneg hlogx.le e
    have hll : (0 : ℝ) ≤ Real.log (Real.log x) := Real.log_nonneg hlog1
    rw [pow_one] at hsm
    have hprod : (Real.log x) ^ (-a₀) * Real.log x = (Real.log x) ^ (1 - a₀) := by
      rw [show (1 : ℝ) - a₀ = -a₀ + 1 by ring, Real.rpow_add hlogx, Real.rpow_one]
    have hmul := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hsm hlogx.le
    have hid : (Real.log x) ^ (-a₀) * Real.log (Real.log x) * Real.log x
        = (Real.log x) ^ (1 - a₀) * Real.log (Real.log x) := by
      rw [← hprod]
      ring
    rw [hid] at hmul
    have hDfrac : D * (s / (4 * (D + 1))) ≤ s / 4 := by
      have hpos : (0 : ℝ) < 4 * (D + 1) := by positivity
      rw [← mul_div_assoc, div_le_div_iff₀ hpos (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 4)]
      nlinarith [hD, hs]
    have hkey : D * (Real.log x) ^ (1 - a₀) * Real.log (Real.log x) ≤ s / 4 * Real.log x := by
      nlinarith [hmul, hD, hlogx, hDfrac]
    have hprod2 : (Real.log x) ^ (b₂ - 1) * Real.log x = (Real.log x) ^ b₂ := by
      have h1 : (Real.log x) ^ b₂ = (Real.log x) ^ (b₂ - 1) * (Real.log x) ^ (1 : ℝ) := by
        rw [← Real.rpow_add hlogx]
        congr 1
        ring
      rw [h1, Real.rpow_one]
    have hbkey : (Real.log x) ^ b₂ ≤ s / 4 * Real.log x := by
      have := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hbm hlogx.le
      rw [hprod2] at this
      linarith
    have hxs : x ^ s = Real.exp (s * Real.log x) := by
      rw [Real.rpow_def_of_pos hx0]
      congr 1
      ring
    have hcl : cardLength b₂ x = Real.exp ((Real.log x) ^ b₂) := rfl
    rw [hxs, hcl]
    have hdiv : (Real.log x) ^ e * Real.exp (D * (Real.log x) ^ (1 - a₀) * Real.log (Real.log x))
          * Real.exp ((Real.log x) ^ b₂) / Real.exp (s * Real.log x)
        = (Real.log x) ^ e
          * Real.exp (D * (Real.log x) ^ (1 - a₀) * Real.log (Real.log x)
            + (Real.log x) ^ b₂ - s * Real.log x) := by
      rw [Real.exp_sub, Real.exp_add]
      ring
    rw [hdiv]
    have hexple : Real.exp (D * (Real.log x) ^ (1 - a₀) * Real.log (Real.log x)
          + (Real.log x) ^ b₂ - s * Real.log x)
        ≤ Real.exp (-(s / 2 * (Real.log x) ^ (1 : ℝ))) := by
      rw [Real.rpow_one]
      exact Real.exp_le_exp.2 (by linarith)
    exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hexple hnn

theorem tendsto_xiMassExactEntropyScaledEnvelope_zero
    {σ q : ℝ} (hwall : 1 < 3 * σ * q * xiWardZeroFreeMarginC / 13) :
    Tendsto (xiMassExactEntropyScaledEnvelope σ q) atTop (𝓝 0)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  let C : ℝ := xiZeroCountEnvelopeConstant
  let D : ℝ := C + 1
  let α : ℝ := 3 * σ * q * xiWardZeroFreeMarginC / 13
  let β : ℝ := α - 1
  have hC : 0 < C := by dsimp only [C]; exact xiZeroCountEnvelopeConstant_pos
  have hD : 0 < D := by dsimp only [D]; linarith
  have hα : 1 < α := by simpa only [α] using hwall
  have hβ : 0 < β := by dsimp only [β]; linarith
  have hβ0 : β ≠ 0 := hβ.ne'
  have haff : Tendsto (fun B : ℝ => 2 * B + 9) atTop atTop :=
    tendsto_atTop_add_const_right atTop 9
      (tendsto_id.const_mul_atTop (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 2))
  have hLtop : Tendsto (fun B : ℝ => Real.log (2 * B + 9)) atTop atTop :=
    Real.tendsto_log_atTop.comp haff
  have hβLtop : Tendsto (fun B : ℝ => β * Real.log (2 * B + 9)) atTop atTop :=
    hLtop.const_mul_atTop hβ
  have hraw := (Real.tendsto_pow_mul_exp_neg_atTop_nhds_zero 1).comp hβLtop
  have hdecay : Tendsto (fun B : ℝ =>
      D * Real.log (2 * B + 9) *
        Real.exp (-β * Real.log (2 * B + 9))) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
    have hmul := Filter.Tendsto.const_mul (D / β) hraw
    have hmul' : Tendsto (fun B : ℝ =>
        (D / β) * ((β * Real.log (2 * B + 9)) *
          Real.exp (-(β * Real.log (2 * B + 9))))) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
      simpa only [Function.comp_apply, pow_one, mul_zero] using hmul
    convert hmul' using 1
    · funext B
      field_simp [hβ0]
  apply squeeze_zero'
  · filter_upwards [eventually_gt_atTop (0 : ℝ)] with B hB
    unfold xiMassExactEntropyScaledEnvelope
    have hlog : 0 ≤ Real.log (2 * B + 4) := Real.log_nonneg (by linarith)
    positivity
  · filter_upwards [eventually_gt_atTop (0 : ℝ)] with B hB
    let x : ℝ := 2 * B + 9
    let y : ℝ := 2 * B + 4
    let L : ℝ := Real.log x
    have hx : 0 < x := by dsimp only [x]; linarith
    have hy : 0 < y := by dsimp only [y]; linarith
    have hL0 : 0 ≤ L := by
      dsimp only [L]
      exact Real.log_nonneg (by dsimp only [x]; linarith)
    have hCD : C ≤ D := by dsimp only [D]; linarith
    have hfac0 : 0 ≤ 2 * B + 3 := by linarith
    have hfac : 2 * B + 3 ≤ x := by dsimp only [x]; linarith
    have hlogy0 : 0 ≤ Real.log y := Real.log_nonneg (by dsimp only [y]; linarith)
    have hlogyx : Real.log y ≤ L := by
      dsimp only [L]
      exact Real.log_le_log hy (by dsimp only [x, y]; linarith)
    have hP :
        C * (2 * B + 3) * Real.log y * Real.exp (-α * L) ≤
          D * x * L * Real.exp (-α * L) := by
      gcongr
    have hxexp : Real.exp L = x := by
      dsimp only [L]
      exact Real.exp_log hx
    have hcombine : D * x * L * Real.exp (-α * L) =
        D * L * Real.exp (-β * L) := by
      rw [← hxexp]
      rw [show D * Real.exp L * L * Real.exp (-α * L) =
          D * L * (Real.exp L * Real.exp (-α * L)) by ring]
      rw [← Real.exp_add]
      congr 2
      dsimp only [β]
      ring
    unfold xiMassExactEntropyScaledEnvelope
    change C * (2 * B + 3) * Real.log y * Real.exp (-α * L) ≤
      D * L * Real.exp (-β * L)
    exact hP.trans_eq hcombine
  · exact hdecay

    kaiserEdgeTransformBoundAt D ≤ 2 * Real.exp (1 + Real.sqrt D)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  rcases hD.eq_or_lt with rfl | hDpos
  · rw [kaiserEdgeTransformBoundAt_zero, Real.sqrt_zero]
    have : (1 : ℝ) ≤ Real.exp 1 := by
      simpa using Real.add_one_le_exp 1
    simpa only [add_zero, mul_one] using
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left this (show (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2 by norm_num)
  have hv : 0 < Real.sqrt D := Real.sqrt_pos.mpr hDpos
  by_cases hv1 : 1 ≤ Real.sqrt D
  · have hsinh : Real.sinh (Real.sqrt D) ≤ Real.exp (Real.sqrt D) := by
      rw [Real.sinh_eq]
      have hexpneg : 0 < Real.exp (-Real.sqrt D) := Real.exp_pos _
      have hexppos : 0 < Real.exp (Real.sqrt D) := Real.exp_pos _
      linarith
    have hdiv : Real.sinh (Real.sqrt D) / Real.sqrt D ≤
        Real.exp (Real.sqrt D) := by
      rw [div_le_iff₀ hv]
      have hmul : Real.exp (Real.sqrt D) ≤
          Real.exp (Real.sqrt D) * Real.sqrt D := by
        exact le_mul_of_one_le_right (Real.exp_pos _).le hv1
      exact hsinh.trans hmul
    have hexp : Real.exp (Real.sqrt D) ≤ Real.exp (1 + Real.sqrt D) :=
      Real.exp_le_exp.mpr (by linarith)
    rw [kaiserEdgeTransformBoundAt_eq_sinh hDpos]
    calc
      2 * Real.sinh (Real.sqrt D) / Real.sqrt D =
          2 * (Real.sinh (Real.sqrt D) / Real.sqrt D) := by ring
      _ ≤ 2 * Real.exp (Real.sqrt D) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hdiv (show (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2 by norm_num)
      _ ≤ 2 * Real.exp (1 + Real.sqrt D) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hexp (show (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2 by norm_num)
  · have hvle : Real.sqrt D ≤ 1 := le_of_not_ge hv1
    have hDle : D ≤ 1 := by
      have hsq := Real.sq_sqrt hDpos.le
      nlinarith
    have hmono := tsum_oddFactorial_mono hD hDle
    have hone : kaiserEdgeTransformBoundAt 1 = 2 * Real.sinh 1 := by
      rw [kaiserEdgeTransformBoundAt_eq_sinh (by norm_num)]
      norm_num
    have hsinh : Real.sinh 1 ≤ Real.exp 1 := by
      rw [Real.sinh_eq]
      have hexpneg : 0 < Real.exp (-1) := Real.exp_pos _
      have hexppos : 0 < Real.exp 1 := Real.exp_pos _
      linarith
    have hexpmono : Real.exp 1 ≤ Real.exp (1 + Real.sqrt D) :=
      Real.exp_le_exp.mpr (by have := Real.sqrt_nonneg D; linarith)
    change kaiserEdgeTransformBoundAt D ≤ kaiserEdgeTransformBoundAt 1 at hmono
    calc
      kaiserEdgeTransformBoundAt D ≤ kaiserEdgeTransformBoundAt 1 := hmono
      _ = 2 * Real.sinh 1 := hone
      _ ≤ 2 * Real.exp 1 := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hsinh (by norm_num)
      _ ≤ 2 * Real.exp (1 + Real.sqrt D) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hexpmono (by norm_num)

prose.text:
# Xi critical kernel: separated real-packet positivity at every rank

- **ID:** `xi-critical-kernel-separated-real-packet-positivity`
- **Stage:** 1-in-progress
- **Type:** OWN THEOREM (unconditional stratum of the live Bezoutian RH endpoint)
- **Sibling:** `theta-kernel-cp-deficit-domination` (CP-1 closed the auxiliary kernel's separated
  packets; this card closes separated packets of the *literal endpoint matrix family*).

## Exact frontier (Gate 1)

Internal. The live endpoint `riemannHypothesis_iff_posSemidef_thetaTailFirstMomentBezoutian`
(`RHTower/ThetaTailFirstMomentDoubleLaplace.lean:817`) states: RH ⟺ the matrices
`[thetaTailFirstMomentBezoutian W_j (conj W_k)]` are PSD for every finite node system in
`{Re W > 1/2}`. The corpus owns, unconditionally:

- `re_logDeriv_xiCent_pos` (`XiEulerSafeCauchyLoss`): `Re L(W) > 0` on `Re W > 1/2`,
  `L = logDeriv xiCent` — the n = 1 stratum at every complex node (with
  `criticalLogDerivKernel_self_re_nonneg_of_half_lt`).
- `xiSquaredEulerFullKernel_twoPoint_det_pos` + `twoMode_twoChannelKernel_realRay_energy_nonneg`
  (`XiSquaredEulerRayFullResponse`, `ThetaCuspTiltFluxWeilParityEulerRayWeld`): the n = 2 stratum
  at all real node pairs `1/2 < x < y` (all gaps), via the two response monotonicities.
- `ThetaCuspTiltFluxThreeRealDeterminant`: n = 3 real nodes *reduced* to the cubic determinant —
  OPEN. The corpus's own boundary marker: "an RH-detecting negative packet … must use either
  complex-node geometry or at least three real-ray modes."
- `XiSquaredEulerDiagonalCorrelationUniversalityLaw`: all-finite-central-minor nonnegativity is
  exactly RH — so the full real-node stratum carries RH content; any unconditional theorem must
  stay away from the tight regime.
- `xiCentBezoutian_eq_mul_criticalKernel`: B(W, conj V) = ξ(W)·conj ξ(V)·K₀(W,V) with
  `K₀ = criticalLogDerivKernel` — congruence transfer between the Bezoutian family and K₀.
- Theta representation: `thetaBilateralLaplace_eq_xiCent`, `thetaBilateralLaplaceMoment_eq_deriv_xiCent`:
  on the real ray, ξ(1/2+β) = ∫_ℝ Φ e^{βx} dx and ξ'(1/2+β) = ∫_ℝ xΦ e^{βx} dx with
  Φ = `thetaCuspFullSource` > 0, even, with the Hedenmalm envelopes
  `C_l E ≤ Φ ≤ C_u E`, `E(x) = e^{9x/2}e^{−πe^{2x}}` on the positive axis.

External. Literature on positivity of Re ξ'/ξ is single-point: classical Re ξ'/ξ > 0 for
Re s ≥ 1 (zero pairing), Hinkkanen/Lagarias-type criteria (RH ⟺ positivity down to the critical
line), and two recent notes on the near-critical strip (arXiv:2201.08599, arXiv:2509.18963).
The coincident-pair limit of the 2×2 minor is the Laguerre/Turán inequality lineage
(Csordas–Norfolk–Varga), proved by the same theta-moment method. No multi-node matrix stratum of
a ξ-Bezoutian/log-derivative kernel is stated anywhere we found. Residue: n ≥ 3 real nodes,
any unconditional regime.

## Structural frame (new, this card)

At real nodes x, y > 1/2 the critical kernel is
`K₀(x,y) = (r(x)+r(y))/(x+y)`, `r(β) = ξ'/ξ(1/2+β)`, with diagonal `K₀(x,x) = r(x)/x`. Hence

`K₀(x,y)/√(K₀(x,x)K₀(y,y)) = cosh(Δ_r/2)/cosh(Δ_β/2)`,
`Δ_r = log r(y) − log r(x)`, `Δ_β = log y − log x`.

So: **the 2×2 real-node minors are PSD exactly when log r is 1-Lipschitz in log β** — the corpus's
two monotonicities (response decreasing, radius-weighted response increasing) are exactly the
slope-in-[0,1] statement, and the corpus's own counterexample (the Herglotz function 1/(w−a),
log-slope < −1) is exactly a Lipschitz violation. Under RH, `r(β) ≈ (2+γ−log4π)·2β` near
β = 1/2: the Lipschitz bound saturates at the Euler edge — the real-node RH content lives at the
edge/close-ratio regime, so an unconditional theorem must take a base R₀ and ratio separation.
[CONJECTURE, recorded for later cycles — LOG-LIP: log r is 1-Lipschitz in log β on all of
(1/2,∞); it is RH-necessary (2×2 minors) and would close every real 2×2 minor. Not claimed.]

## The claim (Gate 2)

**BZ-1.** With `γ := C_u/C_l`, define the explicit constants
`R_u := πe⁴ + log γ + 12`, `R_l := (2π)²e^{2e+8} + 4·log(8γ) + 16`, `R₀ := R_u + R_l`.
(The `2e+8` exponent gives the slack `(b/4)(log b − 2log 2π − 2e) ≥ 2b`, which absorbs the
`(9/8)log b + log(log b) + log 8γ` bookkeeping in (B) with room.)
For every n, every real node sequence `x : ℕ → ℝ` with `x 0 ≥ R₀` and `x(m+1) ≥ R₀²·x(m)`:

1. the matrix `[criticalLogDerivKernel (x j) (x k)]_{j,k<n}` is PSD (complex PosSemidef), and
2. the matrix `[thetaTailFirstMomentBezoutian (x j) (conj (x k))]_{j,k<n}` is PSD —
   an arbitrary-rank unconditional stratum of the literal RH-equivalent endpoint family.

Unconditional, premise-free. New at every n ≥ 3 (corpus owns n ≤ 2; literature owns n = 1).

# Differential-field non-identifiability of the real-zero property

- **ID:** differential-field-real-zero-nonidentifiability
- **Stage:** 5-failed
- **Type:** INSIGNIFICANT
- **Source:** user-directed HT/RH synthesis across `HTGeometry`, `RHTower`, and publication-ready papers
- **Statement:** In the class of even real entire hypertranscendental functions, the real-zero property is not determined by the generated differential field: one explicit Gamma reciprocal has only real zeros, while every finite symmetric nonreal divisor surgery generates exactly the same differential field.

## Goal

Decide whether hypertranscendental differential-field information can carry an RH-type
critical-line conclusion. In the spectral coordinate \(z=-i(s-\tfrac12)\), RH is a real-zero
statement. The target theorem would prove a sharp obstruction: differential-birational data alone
cannot distinguish the real-zero phase, even after imposing entire-ness, evenness, Schwarz
symmetry, and hypertranscendence. The positive survivor would classify the missing datum as a
divisor-sensitive invariant rather than a differential-field invariant.

## Gates

- [x] 0 → 1 in-progress: exact explicit candidate; source-pure; hostile attack and literature audit specified
- [ ] 1 → 2 fully-proven: dependency-closed proof of analytic, divisor, symmetry, hypertranscendence, and field-equality statements
- [ ] 2 → 3 formalized: exact Lean theorem; target module green; axiom and lint gates pass
- [ ] 3 → 4 publication-ready: standalone paper passes hostile general-journal significance review

## Exact live conjecture

Let
\[
\Phi(z)=\bigl(\Gamma(z+\tfrac13)\Gamma(-z+\tfrac13)\bigr)^{-1}.
\]
For every nonzero even real polynomial \(P\), set \(\Phi_P=P\Phi\).

1. \(\Phi\) and \(\Phi_P\) are even real entire functions.
2. \(\Phi\) is hypertranscendental over \(\mathbb C(z)\), with zero set exactly
   \(\{\pm(n+\tfrac13):n\in\mathbb N\}\).
3. \(\mathbb C(z)\langle\Phi_P\rangle=\mathbb C(z)\langle\Phi\rangle\).
4. \(\Phi_P\) has only real zeros exactly when \(P\) has only real zeros.
5. Consequently, choosing \(P=1\) and choosing any even real polynomial with a nonreal symmetric
   zero packet gives opposite real-zero phases inside the same generated differential field.
6. More strongly, every finite conjugation- and sign-stable nonreal divisor packet can be inserted

# Residual differential independence of countable translate families

- **ID:** `residual-countable-translate-differential-independence`
- **Stage:** 5-failed / retired as new scientific knowledge
- **Type:** THEOREM (paper) / GENERIC HT TRANSLATION BRIDGE
- **Scientific status:** `[PROVED HERE] [PROJECT-LOCAL REDISCOVERY] [NOT NEW SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE]`
- **Significance score:** `not 90/100`; current evidence supports a specialist theorem, not a
  field-changing result
- **Statement:** For every discrete infinite real support, every positive summable base-mass
  sequence, and every prescribed countable set of distinct complex translations, a dense residual
  set of bounded positive mass gauges produces a meromorphic Herglotz function whose translated
  family is differentially algebraically independent over `C(z)`.

## The theorem

Let `lambda_n` be distinct real numbers with `|lambda_n| -> infinity`, let `b_n > 0` with
`sum b_n < infinity`, and let `H subset C` be countable. For `u in l-infinity(N,R)`, define

```text
f_u(z) = sum_n b_n exp(u_n)/(lambda_n-z).
```

There is a dense residual set `G_H` of gauges such that

```text
(f_u(z+h))_(h in H)
```

is differentially algebraically independent over `C(z)` for every `u in G_H`. Every `f_u` maps
the upper half-plane into itself.

## Complete paper proof

### 1. Finite real Cauchy-jet controllability

At finitely many distinct upper-half-plane nodes and finitely many jet orders, the vectors

```text
((lambda_n-zeta_j)^(-k))_(j,k)
```

span the complete complex jet space as a real vector space. If a real functional annihilated all
of them, a rational function would have purely imaginary values at infinitely many real support
points. Adding its reflected conjugate produces a rational function with infinitely many zeros.
The upper- and lower-half-plane pole sets are disjoint, so all principal parts vanish.

Choose finitely many support indices giving a surjective real-linear mass-to-jet map. A surjective
finite-dimensional real-linear map is open. Exponential gauge coordinates are local
diffeomorphisms onto open intervals of positive masses. Hence every sufficiently small gauge ball
moves the actual finite jet packet through a full real neighbourhood while preserving positivity.

### 2. Coefficient-uniform relation escape

Fix finitely many translates and jets, distinct differential monomials `M_r`, and a polynomial
coefficient-degree bound `q`. The functions `z^d M_r(x)` are linearly independent polynomials.
Choose `s(q+1)` upper evaluation pairs so that their square evaluation determinant is a nonzero
polynomial in the target jet packets.

Local openness lets every gauge neighbourhood reach a real-open set of packets. A nonzero complex
polynomial cannot vanish on such a set, so the nonvanishing gauges are dense. Uniform summable
majorants on bounded gauge balls give continuity, hence this set is open.

### 3. Baire argument and identity continuation

There are countably many finite relation patterns. Intersect their open dense escape sets in the
complete space `l-infinity(N,R)`. A differential relation over `C(z)` clears to one enumerated
polynomial-coefficient pattern and contradicts its invertible evaluation matrix.

If a relation is initially stated only as an upper-half-plane germ identity, all functions are
globally meromorphic, so the meromorphic identity theorem extends it to the fixed evaluation
nodes. This closes the domain gap identified by the referee.

# Finite-Codimension Landscape RH Nonselection

- **ID:** finite-codimension-landscape-rh-nonselection
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM (paper) / landscape-proof guardrail
- **Source:** `rh-landscape-proof-gate.md`; finite-probe nonselection
- **Statement:** No constraint landscape that is finite-codimensional in the
  even-polynomial perturbation directions can select RH. If the landscape contains
  `Xi(t)=xi(1/2+i t)` and is locally thick along a finite-codimension polynomial-tail
  subspace, then it also contains even real order-one entire functions with off-line
  zero quartets.

## Setup

Let

`Xi(t)=xi(1/2+i t)=Phi(t^2)`.

Let `U` be a real vector subspace of `R[u]` of finite codimension. Think of

`Xi(t) + R(t^2)`, `R in U`,

as the local polynomial-tail slice of a proposed constraint landscape. Finite
Taylor conditions, finitely many moment/value/passport conditions, and finite
symbolic audits all cut out such finite-codimension slices.

For a fixed `N>=0`, impose seam-jet preservation by replacing `U` with

`U_N = U cap u^(N+1) R[u]`.

This is still finite-codimensional inside `u^(N+1) R[u]`, hence infinite-dimensional.

## Theorem

For every finite-codimensional real subspace `U <= R[u]` and every `N>=0`, there are
a non-real `u0` and a polynomial `R in U cap u^(N+1) R[u]` such that:

1. `R(u0)=-Phi(u0)`;
2. for either square root `tau` of `u0`,

   `F(t)=Xi(t)+R(t^2)`

   is even, real on the real axis, entire of order `1`, agrees with `Xi` through
   derivatives `0,...,2N+1` at `t=0`, belongs to the finite-codimension landscape
   slice, and has the non-real zero quartet
   `tau,-tau,conj(tau),-conj(tau)`.

Therefore a finite-codimension local landscape cannot force RH.

## Proof

Since `U_N` is infinite-dimensional, choose linearly independent polynomials
`P,Q in U_N` with `Q != 0`. Then `P/Q` is a nonconstant rational function. As in
finite linear-probe nonselection, there is a non-real `u0` with `Q(u0) != 0` and
`P(u0)/Q(u0) notin R`: otherwise the rational function `P/Q` would be real-valued
on a nonempty open subset of the upper half-plane, contradicting the open mapping
theorem.

Thus `P(u0)` and `Q(u0)` span `C` over `R`. Choose real `a,b` with

`aP(u0)+bQ(u0)=-Phi(u0)`.

Set

`R=aP+bQ`.

Then `R in U_N`, so the finite-codimension landscape constraints and the seam-jet
vanishing are preserved. Defining

`F(t)=Xi(t)+R(t^2)`

gives an even real entire function of order `1`. The order is still `1` because a
polynomial cannot cancel the non-polynomial order-one function `Xi`. Since `R` is
divisible by `u^(N+1)`, the perturbation `R(t^2)` vanishes to order `2N+2` at the
seam. Finally, with `tau^2=u0`,

`F(tau)=Phi(u0)+R(u0)=0`,

and evenness plus real symmetry gives the full quartet. Since `u0` is non-real, this
quartet is off the real `t`-axis, so `F` violates RH.

## Consequence for the RH Route

The user-level slogan "prove the landscape, not a generator" has a precise negative
edge:

> The landscape cannot be a finite-codimension constraint around `Xi` in local
> polynomial-tail directions.

Any such landscape is too thick; it contains false-nearby functions with the same
finite local/passport data and with off-line zeros. A viable RH landscape must be
infinite-codimensional/all-order in exactly the sense supplied by a genuine Euler
product, the completed explicit formula as a full distributional identity, a
geometric polarization, or an equivalent source rigidity theorem.

Thus the next proof obligation is not a finite extra condition on the rank-one Weyl
chart. It is an all-order source theorem that prevents these polynomial-tail
perturbations before zero-location language appears.

## Source Boundary

significance is methodological: it rules out a class of landscape-shaped but finite
constraint proposals. It does not preserve the Euler product; the fact that Euler
product structure is destroyed is precisely why the Euler product must be part of any

For real `a,b,x,y,delta_a,delta_b`:

```text
(a*y+b)-(a*x+b) = a*(y-x),
0<a -> (a*x+b<a*y+b <-> x<y),
0<a -> (a*x+b=a*y+b <-> x=y),
x≠y -> ((delta_a*x+delta_b)-(delta_a*y+delta_b))/(y-x) = -delta_a.
```

For real horizontal displacement `a` and vertical displacement `tau`, the reflected pair and
full quartet satisfy

```text
(-a+i*tau)^(-2) + (a+i*tau)^(-2)

quartetCurvature(a,tau)
  = 4*(a^2-tau^2)/(a^2+tau^2)^2,

0<a -> (0<quartetCurvature(a,tau) <-> |tau|<a).
```

/-
The resonance method cannot produce a power.

Every known `Ω`-result for `max |ζ(1/2+it)|` comes from the resonance method, whose entire gain is
the maximal Gál sum.  Bondarenko and Seip evaluated that maximum:

    Γ(N) = exp((C + o(1)) · √(log N · loglog N)).

Writing `L = log N`, the gain exponent is `C√(L log L)`, while a power saving `N^c` has exponent
`cL`.  Their difference is

    L · (C·√(log L / L) − c) → −∞,

because `log L / L → 0`.  So the resonance gain is smaller than every fixed power, and the exponent
ratio tends to zero: **no resonance construction can give `Ω(T^c)` for any `c > 0`**.

The module is source-independent: it is a statement about the growth of `√(L log L)` against `L`.
-/
import Mathlib

namespace HTGeometry

open Filter Topology

/-- Bondarenko–Seip exponent of the maximal Gál sum, at `N = exp L`. -/
noncomputable def galSumExponent (C L : ℝ) : ℝ := C * Real.sqrt (L * Real.log L)

theorem log_div_tendsto_zero : Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => Real.log x / x) atTop (nhds 0) := by
  simpa using Real.isLittleO_log_id_atTop.tendsto_div_nhds_zero

theorem sqrt_log_div_tendsto_zero :
    Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => Real.sqrt (Real.log x / x)) atTop (nhds 0) := by
  have h := (Real.continuous_sqrt.tendsto 0).comp log_div_tendsto_zero
  simpa [Function.comp_def] using h

/-- The gain exponent, factored so that the `L`-scale is explicit. -/
theorem galSumExponent_eq (C : ℝ) {L : ℝ} (hL : 0 < L) :
    galSumExponent C L = L * (C * Real.sqrt (Real.log L / L)) := by
  unfold galSumExponent
  have h : Real.sqrt (L * Real.log L) = L * Real.sqrt (Real.log L / L) := by
    have h2 : L * Real.sqrt (Real.log L / L) =
        Real.sqrt (L ^ 2) * Real.sqrt (Real.log L / L) := by
      rw [Real.sqrt_sq hL.le]
    rw [h2, ← Real.sqrt_mul (by positivity)]
    congr 1
    field_simp
  rw [h]
  ring

/-- **The resonance gain is subpolynomial.**  Against any fixed power saving the exponent
difference tends to `-∞`. -/
theorem galSumExponent_sub_atBot (C : ℝ) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) :
    Tendsto (fun L : ℝ => galSumExponent C L - c * L) atTop atBot := by
  have hfac : Tendsto (fun L : ℝ => C * Real.sqrt (Real.log L / L) - c) atTop (nhds (-c)) := by
    have h := (sqrt_log_div_tendsto_zero.const_mul C).sub_const c
    simpa using h
  have hmul : Tendsto (fun L : ℝ => L * (C * Real.sqrt (Real.log L / L) - c)) atTop atBot :=
    Tendsto.atTop_mul_neg (by linarith) tendsto_id hfac
  refine hmul.congr' ?_
  filter_upwards [eventually_gt_atTop (0 : ℝ)] with L hL
  rw [galSumExponent_eq C hL]
  ring

/-- **No resonance construction gives a power.**  The maximal Gál-sum gain divided by any fixed
power tends to zero, so the resonance method cannot produce `Ω(T^c)` for any `c > 0`, and hence no
known method disproves the Lindelöf hypothesis. -/
theorem resonanceGain_tendsto_zero (C : ℝ) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) :
    Tendsto (fun L : ℝ => Real.exp (galSumExponent C L) / Real.exp (c * L))
      atTop (nhds 0) := by
  have h := Real.tendsto_exp_atBot.comp (galSumExponent_sub_atBot C hc)
  simpa [Function.comp_def, Real.exp_sub] using h

end HTGeometry
